Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Seattle WA
821 PM PST Mon Nov 16 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Mostly dry conditions this afternoon as brief ridging moves
through the area. A deep upper low offshore will move southwards 
Wednesday for some spotty showers over the southern half of the
area. Drier conditions Friday before troughing deepens offshore
into next weekend for the return of more precipitation and 
active weather.

&&

.SHORT TERM /TONIGHT THROUGH WEDNESDAY NIGHT/...
Drier conditions this evening with post frontal showers mainly 
offshore. With some light surface gradients tonight into 
Tuesday morning, will likely see areas of fog early Tuesday AM, 
for areas in the Southwest Interior and Central Puget Sound. 
Onshore flow in the afternoon will help the fog dissipate with 
high temperatures generally in the low 50s for most areas. 

A upper level trough offshore will start to dig southwards 
Tuesday into Wednesday. This system will primarily move south of
our area but will rotate showers over the southern half of the
area, additionally along the coast on Wednesday. Along with 
precipitation, easterly winds will kick up slightly, especially in
the Cascade gaps, with probabilities of gusts over 35 MPH 
generally around 40-60% across much of the gaps Wednesday 
morning. High temps will be slightly cooler with upper 40s and 
low 50s, areas along the Southwest Interior and coast could see 
highs in the mid 40s. Overnight lows in the low to mid 30s. 

&&

.LONG TERM /THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...Drier conditions Thursday
into Friday as the aforementioned low rotates southward away
from western Washington. Likely will see areas of fog Friday
morning as residual moisture remains. Upper level troughing and
a upper level low will drop down from the Gulf of Alaska and
will situate itself over the coast into the weekend. Light
precipitation comes back into the forecast over the weekend as 
the low spins showers up in the area. Latest ensemble guidance 
suggests a more active, wetter pattern through the first half of
the week with multiple systems entering the area. 

Mazurkiewicz

&&

.AVIATION...Conditions are predominantly VFR tonight, though 
isolated MVFR cigs will remain possible for terminals along the
coast (KHQM) this evening as showers continue to move inland 
across the Olympic Peninsula. With conditions clearing across 
the interior, fog is expected to develop overnight into Tuesday 
morning, first across the South Sound and Chehalis River Valley 
(impacting KOLM), then later spreading into other portions of 
Puget Sound and resulting in the potential for conditions to 
deteriorate to IFR/LIFR for a few hours early Tuesday morning. 
Conditions will then rebound to VFR by mid-morning as fog 
dissipates. 

KSEA...VFR conditions will continue tonight with southerly 
winds persisting at 3-6 kt. Areas of fog look to develop 
overnight into Tuesday morning and could encroach upon the 
terminal. As a result, conditions may drop down to IFR for a few
hours on Tuesday morning, with latest probabilistic guidance 
hinting at about a 10% chance of IFR conditions developing 
between 12-14Z. 

14

&&

.MARINE...Seas across the coastal waters this evening are still
hovering between 14-16 ft but will continue to subside towards 
10-12 ft by Tuesday morning. Overall, winds remain much lighter 
across the area waters today due to high pressure which has 
built back into the region. Winds will increase through the day 
on Tuesday and will turn offshore by Tuesday night as a low 
pressure system offshore moves southward through the NE Pacific.
Winds will be locally enhanced along the gaps in terrain, most 
notably through the Strait of Juan de Fuca and near Grays Harbor
Tuesday night. Latest REFS guidance shows a 70-90% chance of 
wind gusts exceeding gale force across the outer coastal waters,
so have have gone ahead and issued gale warnings for these 
areas. Gusts may also briefly reach gale along the inner coastal
waters (especially the waters adjacent to the West Entrance of 
the Strait and along Grays Harbor County) but are not expected 
to be as long- lived. Nonetheless, additional small craft 
advisories are likely for the central and western Strait as 
easterly winds increase to 25-30 kt Tuesday night, as well for 
the inner coastal water zones on Tuesday as both winds and seas 
increase. Seas will build back to 12-15 ft Tuesday night into 
early Wednesday.

Calmer conditions will follow on Wednesday as the low pushes 
out of the area and then persist through Friday as high pressure
builds back into the coastal waters in its wake. The pattern
will become more active again heading into the weekend as another
series of systems look to move through the area. 

14

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
The Skokomish River has fallen below flood stage and will 
continue to recede throughout the week. River flooding is not 
expected over the next several days, but chances increase again
early next week (mostly on the Skokomish River) as the pattern
becomes more active and additional rainfall is expected over 
the weekend and into early next week.
